new_items.title: SavedVariables migration v2 for the minimap.shown rename: a stored `shown` folds into LibDBIcon's `hide`, so every player keeps their minimap setting
new_items.change: Required by the owner alongside WS-06's path rename (PF-13), using PF-08's runner. The stored key stays `global.minimap.hide`, and the step is a defensive fold. core/Database.lua: `NS.SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` (was 1 after PF-08). Append one row to SCHEMA_STEPS: `{ to = 2, scope = 'global', apply = function(g) local m = g.minimap; if type(m) ~= 'table' or m.shown == nil then return end; if m.shown == false and not m.hide then m.hide = true end; m.shown = nil end }`. Comment on the row: AceDB strips `hide = false` (the default at defaults/Profile.lua:148) at logout, so a nil `hide` means shown. A stray `shown` key could only come from a raw path write to the new CLI path `global.minimap.shown` before the closure row was registered, or from a hand-edited SavedVariables file. Where both are present, `hide` (LibDBIcon's key) wins unless `shown == false`. Folding and deleting `shown` keeps the anti-pattern #81 rule of one stored state. Run the step on the no-AceDB path too: `g` is sv.global (core/Database.lua:21-27). Update the comment above SCHEMA_STEPS (:30-33): the ladder is no longer empty, and v2 is the minimap.shown rename. defaults/Profile.lua global block comment (:136-140): the CLI path is `global.minimap.shown` and the stored key stays `hide`. Point to the v2 step. docs/schema.md migration section (:85, :112, :117 after PF-08): add a v2 row naming the fold, and state that the stamp after first run is 2. The commit body records that the setting survives the rename.
new_items.tests: Red first in tests/test_database.lua, restoring NS.db.global.minimap and the stamp after each case. (a) With global.schemaVersion = 1, set `minimap = { shown = false }`, run NS:RunMigrations(), and assert `minimap.hide == true`, `minimap.shown == nil` and `schemaVersion == 2`. Comment `-- red under: SCHEMA_STEPS without the v2 row`. (b) `minimap = { hide = true }` with no `shown` (an existing player who hid the button): after migration `hide == true`, and `/pfe get global.minimap.shown` (through the cli harness) answers false. This pins that the rename keeps the setting. (c) `minimap = { shown = true, hide = true }`: `hide` stays true and `shown` is cleared. (d) `minimap = { minimapPos = 200 }`: untouched apart from the stamp, so a dragged position survives. (e) A second RunMigrations is a no-op. Re-pin PF-08's 'InitDB stamps NS.SCHEMA_VERSION' case to 2. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md and the README Tests badge.

new_items.title: SavedVariables migration for the minimap rename: a v3 global-scope step keeps every existing player's button choice across global.minimap.hide -> global.minimap.shown (WS-06)
new_items.change:
PC-13 renames the minimap row's schema/CLI path from global.minimap.hide to global.minimap.shown. Storage stays LibDBIcon's db.global.minimap.hide (launcher-§3, anti-pattern #81). This item adds a versioned migration so every existing player keeps their setting after the rename, and so no second stored 'shown' key can survive next to 'hide'. It lands after PC-03 (the scoped runner) and PC-04 (which takes schema v2).
(1) core/Database.lua:
- SCHEMA_VERSION 2 -> 3.
- Add `migrations[3] = { scope = 'global', run = foldMinimapShown }`.
- `local function foldMinimapShown(global)`: `local mm = global and global.minimap`. If `type(mm) ~= 'table'`, return, so AceDB's declared default `minimap = { hide = false }` materializes as today. If `mm.shown ~= nil`: when `mm.hide == nil`, set `mm.hide = not mm.shown`; then set `mm.shown = nil`. An existing `hide`, and `minimapPos`, are never touched, so `hide` always wins.
- The step is idempotent: a second run finds no `shown` and does nothing. It never assigns the whole `minimap` table, because LibDBIcon keeps minimapPos in it (the Database.lua :20-26 rule).
- Keep the step at CCN 5 or below.
(2) core/Database.lua header comment (:20-33). Replace 'no schemaVersion bump: this is a new default, not a stored-path move' with the v3 note: the row's PATH moved to global.minimap.shown (WS-06), the STORED key stays hide, and v3 folds any stray stored `shown` into `hide` so the player's choice survives. Add the matching migrations-table comment line.
(3) settings/Schema.lua :139-146 and :216-228 comments (already reworded by PC-13): add one sentence pointing at Database migrations[3] as the guarantee that the rename moved no stored value.
(4) Docs:
- docs/schema.md: the minimap row entry notes the v3 migration.
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: the savedvariables / migrations section lists v2 (PC-04's Loot lift) and v3 (the minimap fold).
- README Version History, next release row (owner writes it): '/pc get|set global.minimap.hide is now global.minimap.shown; your minimap button setting is kept.'
- docs/smoke-tests.md: add the upgrade step below as a new T-nn.
new_items.tests:
Red first, in tests/test_database.lua. Each case uses a fresh ctx.loadAddon with a seeded PrettyChatDB. Mark each '-- red under: SCHEMA_VERSION 2 with no migrations[3]'.
(a) 'an existing hidden button stays hidden across the minimap rename'. Seed global = { schemaVersion = 2, minimap = { hide = true, minimapPos = 200 } }. After load: db.global.minimap.hide == true, minimapPos == 200, db.global.schemaVersion == 3, and Schema.Get('global.minimap.shown') == false.
(b) 'a stray stored shown key is folded into hide and removed'. Seed minimap = { shown = false }: hide == true and shown == nil. Seed minimap = { shown = true }: hide is false or nil, and shown == nil.
(c) 'hide wins over a conflicting stray shown'. Seed { hide = true, shown = true }: hide == true, shown == nil.
(d) 'the v3 step is idempotent'. Run Database.RunMigrations a second time and nothing changes.
(e) 'a fresh install still stamps 3 and shows the button'.
The existing :59 ahead-stamp normalization case stays green. Regenerate docs/test-cases.md (`lua5.1 tests/run.lua --list > docs/test-cases.md`) and the README Tests badge in this commit.

new_items.smoke: In-client upgrade check, on an install whose minimap button was hidden before the update: install the new build and /reload. The button stays hidden. `/pc get global.minimap.shown` prints false and the General > Master controls 'Minimap button' checkbox is unticked. Then `/pc set global.minimap.shown true` brings the button back at its old dragged position (minimapPos kept). /reload again, and it stays shown.

mapped.amend_change: Upstream follow-up LK-23 (WhatGroup#22 adoption note) is this item: LibKa0s-Schema-1.0 minor 2 with the writeThrough descriptor field must be in the RV-WG payload, and WhatGroup deliberately passes NO writeThrough list (the owner's route (b) under WS-02). On a library-absent load /wg enable, /wg disable and /wg test on|off print the WS-02 library-absent line ('/wg enable is unavailable: the LibKa0s library did not load.') and raise no Lua error. The two tests/test_libka0s.lua characterization cases are rewritten to assert that line and the unchanged store, and the options-ui-§1 SHOULD deviation row is recorded in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. HostSchemaStub copies LK-23's referenceStub (which gains writeThrough) but leaves writeThrough unset.

Upstream follow-up WS-06 (WHATGROUP-R-15, launcher-§3 at v2.65.0) is this item. SavedVariables carry-over (required by the owner so existing players keep their minimap setting): the stored key stays db.global.minimap.hide, as WS-06 requires, so no stored value moves. The rename still ships a guarded migration step, which also depends on WG-08's step-driven runner. In core/Database.lua, bump NS.SCHEMA_VERSION to 2 and add NS.MIGRATIONS[2] = function(db): local m = db.global and db.global.minimap; if m and m.shown ~= nil then if m.hide == nil then m.hide = not m.shown end; m.shown = nil end. This folds any stray stored `shown` key (anti-pattern #81, e.g. from a dev build or a hand-edited SV) into LibDBIcon's hide and deletes it, and it never touches minimapPos. The step is idempotent and a no-op for the ordinary store. The same step also deletes the dead profile-scoped branch, walking raw WhatGroupDB.profiles[*].global.minimap per WS-03; it is the branch the Schema.lua:613 comment names. docs/schema.md records the v2 step. Extra tests in tests/test_database.lua: (1) 'database: a pre-rename SV with global.minimap.hide = true boots with global.minimap.shown reading false and the button hidden', which boots from a raw v1 SV { global = { schemaVersion = 1, minimap = { hide = true, minimapPos = 200 } } } and asserts H.Get('global.minimap.shown') == false, db.global.minimap.hide == true, minimapPos == 200 and schemaVersion == 2. (2) 'database: a stray stored minimap.shown folds into hide and is removed', where { shown = false } gives hide == true, shown == nil and the step re-run is a no-op. Extra smoke: before updating, hide the button with the old build, then install the new build and /reload. The button stays hidden, and /wg get global.minimap.shown answers false.

critique.problem: The pre-re-vendor ordering is backwards in the dependency graph. The item text, the plan_notes and 03_SPEC.md:195-207 ('Lands before or with RV' table) all say these fixes land BEFORE the addon's RV commit so the re-vendor commit is green. AM-01 says 'RUNS BEFORE RV-AM'. CM-01 says 'RV-CM depends on it'. BL-01 and BL-02 say 'LANDS BEFORE RV-BL'. KC-01 says 'LANDS BEFORE RV-KC'. WG-01 says it 'must land BEFORE the re-vendor'. Yet every one of these items lists RV-x in depends_on, and no RV item lists any of them. A scheduler that follows depends_on will run each re-vendor first, and the RV commit will be red (lone CR at AuraMaster tests/page_helpers.lua:80, the prose-gate spellings in ConsumableMaster and KickCD, BankLedger's wow_mock C_Timer no-op, WhatGroup's SetItemRef callback). That breaks the spec's 'SG steps 1-3 are green at the RV commit itself'. The same gap covers the SetMany stub halves the spec lists as 'before or with RV': LH has no pre-RV item at all (LH-15 depends on RV-LH), and PM-01, PC-01, AT-01, PF-05 and PF-06 all depend on their RV. The RV change text ('the fixes are this addon's M3 items') contradicts the spec too.
critique.fix: For each pre-fix, remove RV-x from depends_on and depend on LK-33 plus the specific LK item instead (AM-01: LK-06, LK-33; BL-02: LK-22, LK-33; CM-01: LK-07, LK-33; KC-01: LK-07, LK-13, LK-33; WG-01: LK-33). Then add the pre-fixes to the RV item: RV-AM gets AM-01 and AM-02, RV-BL gets BL-01 and BL-02, RV-CM gets CM-01, RV-KC gets KC-01, RV-WG gets WG-01. Fold these into the RV commit by name: WG-02 into RV-WG; the SetMany stub half of AT-01, PM-01 and PC-01 into RV-AT, RV-PM and RV-PC; PF-05 and PF-06 into RV-PF (or make RV-PF depend on them); and a minimal LH stub SetMany into RV-LH. Rewrite the RV change text to name its pre-fixes, and drop the sentence 'fixes are this addon's M3 items'. Consider re-milestoning the pre-fixes to M2.

critique.where: WA-01 (pre-flight check and dry-run), CM-28 (the note about the frozen v1.55.0 bundle), WS-01 (vendored-side loop), BL-23 / PC-25 / WG-29 / CM-28 / LH-34 (span lists)
critique.problem: Every addon had a kit-only re-vendor of v1.54.2 that touched only tests/_kit/: AuraMaster 329e1a3, ConsumableMaster 1f86d4e, BankLedger 6b12edf, PrettyChat 8421342 and WhatGroup 7f38ddd. At each of those commits CLAUDE.md reads v1.54.2, so every addon's frozen 2026-09-23-v1.55.0 bundle is right to say 'v1.54.2 -> v1.55.0'. Three parts of the plan get this wrong. (1) WA-01 says its pre-flight 'finds AuraMaster's v1.54.2-for-v1.53.0 base', and its dry-run expects v1.53.0 as the base. That contradicts AM-02 and raw_plan's cluster note ('AuraMaster's v1.55.0 base note is correct (kit-only v1.54.2) and must not be corrected'). WA-01's cross-check `git log -1 -- libs/LibKa0s` cannot see kit-only re-vendors, so the pre-flight would flag all eleven addons and invite false 'correction' notes. (2) CM-28 tells the implementer to note that the frozen v1.55.0 bundle's v1.54.2 base disagrees with a previous tag of v1.53.0, which is false. critique.where: Span-bundle line-1 grammar: BL-23, CM-28, PC-25, WG-29, LH-34, PM-18, AM-02 vs WS-01 (4)
critique.problem: WS-01 defines line 1 as exactly `Delta: LibKa0s v<A> -> v<B> (span: v<A> v<...> v<B>)`, with the folder named -v<A>-v<B>. The items differ from that and from each other. CM-28 uses a non-tag base 'v1.17.x'. BL-23 names v1.15.0 -> v1.54.2 in a folder named -v1.18.0-v1.53.0, with a span ending at v1.53.0. LH-34 uses v1.15.0 -> v1.53.0, PM-18 uses v1.16.0 -> v1.54.2, and PC-25 and WG-29 use v1.18.0 -> v1.53.0. Some separate the span with commas and some with spaces. The amended recorded-side loop greps every vX.Y.Z on line 1, so bases like v1.15.0 get counted as recorded, and 'v1.17.x' is silently dropped.
critique.fix: Normalize every span item to WS-01's exact grammar: A = first unrecorded tag, B = last (v1.54.2 per the kit-only issue), the folder named -v<A>-v<B>, and a space-separated span. Put the true previous base in the body, not on line 1.

critique.where: LH-13 (amend: MIGRATIONS to=9), PC-27 (foldMinimapShown), WG-11 (amend: NS.MIGRATIONS[2])
critique.problem: The fold only runs `hide = not shown` when `hide == nil`. Every one of these addons declares `minimap = { hide = false }` as a default: LootHistory/defaults/Global.lua:63, PrettyChat/core/Database.lua:37 and WhatGroup/settings/Schema.lua:610 (BuildDefaults). AceDB's copyDefaults, and the kit's faithful copy at tests/_kit/mock_record.lua:173-195, fills `hide = false` into db.global at AceDB:New. That happens before RunMigrations, so `hide` is never nil when the step runs. The branch can't be reached, and a stray `shown = false` is dropped while hide stays false, so the player's hidden button comes back. Each item's own red-first test then fails for good: LH-13 (e) `{shown=false}` gives hide == true, PC-27 (b) seeds `{shown=false}` and expects hide == true, and WG-11 test (2) `{shown=false}` gives hide == true.
critique.fix: Use PF-26's rule, which is correct under copyDefaults: `if m.shown == false and not m.hide then m.hide = true end; m.shown = nil`, with `hide` winning in every other case. Apply it in LH-13, PC-27 and WG-11. Also add a comment in each step saying that AceDB materializes `hide = false` before the runner, which is why `hide == nil` can't be used as the test.

critique.where: AM-17 vs LK-28 (LibKa0s OptionsTabs RenderTabbedSchema opts)
critique.problem: AM-17 maps AuraMaster's `disabledFor` and `disabledNotice` straight onto LK-28's opts, and its characterization pins must stay green after the swap. One of those pins is the 'disabled state on Bars/Icons/Text'. But LK-28 specifies that disabledNotice 'renders the notice in place of rows when disabledFor answers true'. AuraMaster today draws the notice and then every row disabled (settings/OptionsSetup.lua:624-640, via RenderRows opts.disabled and ctx.__renderDisabled for bespoke tabs), so the pins go red after the swap. AM-17 also depends on 'a tab keyed by a schema group replaces that group's rows, as the v1.56.0 Options doc specifies', which is AuraMaster's collectTabs behavior at :560-580. LK-28 only defines bespoke tabs 'placed before a named group via before' and never specifies replacement. As planned, AM-17 hits its own STOP condition.
critique.fix: Amend LK-28 before it is tagged. `disabledFor` true should draw the notice above the rows and render the rows disabled (RenderRows opts.disabled, plus ctx.__renderDisabled around bespoke render), not replace them. A `tabs` entry whose key equals a schema group should take that group's place in the strip and be handed the group's rows (render(ctx, rows)). Add library tests for both, so AM-17 can adopt without a fork or a re-pin.

critique.where: MM-14 change (2) and the MM-14 amend ('SetByPaths becomes S:SetMany')
critique.problem: The shims are written with colon syntax: `NS.FindSchemaRow = S:FindRow`, `NS.RegisterSchemaRows = S:AddRows`, `NS.GetSetting(path, id) = S:Get(path, id)`, `S:Set`, `S:ApplyDefault`, `S:SetMany(entries, …)`. `NS.X = S:FindRow` is not valid Lua. The LibKa0s-Schema-1.0 instance members are also dot-defined (LibKa0s/Schema.lua:306-607: `function S.Get(path, instanceId)`, `function S.Set(path, value, instanceId)` and so on). A literal `S:Get(path, id)` passes S as `path`. Every other adopter item (PF-11, WG-12, KC-18, AM-15, CM-17) uses dot form.
critique.fix: Rewrite MM-14 and its amend in dot form: `NS.FindSchemaRow = S.FindRow`, `NS.RegisterSchemaRows = function(rows) S.AddRows(rows) end`, `NS.GetSetting = function(p, id) return S.Get(p, id) end`, `NS.SetByPath = S.Set`, `NS.ApplyDefault = function(row, id) return S.ApplyDefault(row, id) end`, and `S.SetMany(entries, { instanceId = windowId, act = …, scope = … })`.

critique.where: WG-11 depends_on (after the reconcile amend)
critique.problem: The amend adds `NS.SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` and `NS.MIGRATIONS[2] = function(db) …` and says the step 'depends on WG-08's step-driven runner'. The only dependency it adds is WS-06, so WG-11's depends_on is ['RV-WG','WS-06']. Today's WhatGroup/core/Database.lua:23-45 has no NS.MIGRATIONS table and just stamps `g.schemaVersion = NS.SCHEMA_VERSION`, so if WG-11 is scheduled before WG-08, the v2 step never runs and its tests can't pass. WG-08's own red test also sets `NS.SCHEMA_VERSION = 2` and `NS.MIGRATIONS[2]`, which collides with WG-11's real v2 step if the order is reversed.
critique.fix: Add WG-08 to WG-11's depends_on. Have WG-08's injected test step use `SCHEMA_VERSION + 1`, taken from the runner, instead of a literal 2, and restore the table afterwards, so it stays valid once WG-11 has taken v2.

critique.where: LH-13 change text (base vs amend)
critique.problem: The base change opens with 'The stored key stays db.global.minimap.hide, so no SavedVariables change and no migration.' The appended amend then requires a MIGRATIONS `{ to = 9 }` step, `NS.SCHEMA_LATEST`, rewriting the literal 8 at tests/test_database.lua:443/449/455/476/486/501/519, and moving LH-12's smoke from 8 to 9. The item contradicts itself, and the verify line (just 'renamed and added cases') doesn't check the migration either. PC-13's and PF-13's texts say the same 'no migration' thing, while PC-27 and PF-26 add one. For PF-13 the amend corrects the sentence; PC-13 is left as it was.
critique.fix: In LH-13, delete 'so no SavedVariables change and no migration' and replace it with 'the stored key is unchanged; a defensive to = 9 fold step is added (below)'. Add `grep -n 'to = 9' core/Database.lua` and the four new test cases to the verify. Reword PC-13 the same way to point at PC-27.

critique.where: PC-27 vs PC-14 (both edit the minimap/defaults comment in PrettyChat core/Database.lua)
critique.problem: PC-27 (2) rewrites 'core/Database.lua header comment (:20-33)' and its 'no schemaVersion bump' sentence. PC-14 deletes Database.defaults (:34-39) and moves that same reasoning from core/Database.lua:16-33 into defaults/Profile.lua. PC-27 depends on PC-03, PC-04 and PC-13 but not PC-14, so the order between them is undefined. If PC-14 lands first, PC-27's target comment is gone. If PC-27 lands first, PC-14 moves a comment that has already been rewritten, and the item text doesn't expect that.
critique.fix: Add PC-14 to PC-27's depends_on, and retarget PC-27 (2) to the moved comment in defaults/Profile.lua (NS.GlobalDefaults) plus the migrations-table comment in core/Database.lua.

critique.where: MM-16 amend ('the v15 migration in core/Database.lua (:52, :850-891)')
critique.problem: Those lines are wrong. CURRENT_DB_VERSION is at MultiMeters/core/Database.lua:53. The step that moves minimap to the global store (v14->v15) is `migrations[14]` at :904, since the runner indexes by the from-version (`migrations[from]`). Lines 850-891 are inside migrations[13]. An implementer following the cite reads the wrong step, and test (f) ('pre-v15 account with profile.minimap.hide=true, run through the migration runner') needs to know it is migrations[14].

critique.where: MM-13 / MM-14 / MM-20 verify ('line-cap awk (no output)')
critique.problem: The verify names a check that isn't written out anywhere in the item, and MultiMeters has no script by that name. Other repos' items spell the command out: `git ls-files '*.lua' | grep -v -e '^libs/' -e '^tests/_kit/' | xargs wc -l | awk '$2!="total" && $1>1500'`. MM-20 in particular depends on it (Row.lua is 1469, test_row.lua 1490).

critique.where: MM-20 change (2) ('peel the cell-clear helpers (:1446-1455) into modules/Row_NameCell.lua's sibling')
critique.problem: modules/Row.lua:1446-1455 is RowProto:Release, not a set of cell-clear helpers. Moving it to a new sibling file also needs a TOC entry and a load-order position, and the item mentions neither. Separately, ApplyLayout today allocates `local live = {}` at Row.lua:1311 on every call. The item says liveCells is 'never reallocated', so this existing allocation has to go, which the item doesn't say.
